memory_candidates.title: Executable #eval conformance probes refute formal-blocker framings cheaply
memory_candidates.content: Three prior research rounds on a Lean tableau attributed a completeness block to an unformalized fuel-sufficiency theorem. A 7-line #eval of the decision procedure on known-valid formulas refuted the target theorem outright in one dispatch, exposing two calculus defects nobody had recorded. For any executable decision procedure in Lean, run it on known-valid and known-invalid inputs BEFORE planning proof work about it.

memory_candidates.title: Island countermodels fail on positive universals, not eventualities
memory_candidates.content: A countermodel extracted from a finite tableau branch over an infinite NoMaxOrder domain (e.g. Z) reads false at every unpopulated point. This SATISFIES negative eventualities (F(Fp)@t) vacuously but FALSIFIES positive universals (T(Gp)@t), since G requires content at every later point. The intuition that 'unfulfilled eventualities are the problem' is inverted. Any finite-branch extraction needs a total extension (lasso/stutter) of branch content to the whole domain.

memory_candidates.title: Check fuel-constant growth rate against its own docstring justification
memory_candidates.content: A fuel bound whose docstring cites a 2^n state-space bound but whose formula is quadratic in n is arithmetically insufficient on its face. Reading the constant's growth rate against its stated justification is a seconds-long check that can settle a 'fuel sufficiency' research question that otherwise reads as open. Confirm empirically by measuring the minimal fuel at which known-valid inputs still close, across a size-indexed family.
